messages:
josh_support: Heads-up — ACME corp reporting p99 latency spike across /v1/generate since ~10:30UTC. Customer sees p99 ~8.2s (norm ~200ms). They say requests are "piling up" at ingress, causing timeouts on their side.

lina_sre: Oof. Any 5xx or 429s showing up in their logs?

josh_support: No 5xx from customer. We're seeing 429s from our admission controller and long queue times. Example from their forwarded log: 
`````
acme-prod | ts=2026-03-17T10:32:41Z level=warn admit=429 queue_len=94 inflight=160 worker_avail=2 p95=600ms p99=8.2s
`````

ana_runtime: Looks like worker saturation + admission backpressure. Which model/pool?

josh_support: hosted region-us-east1, model=redwood-7b-std on dedicated pool acme-prod.

mike_oncall: Paging eng-runtime. @ana_runtime can you check pool autoscaling / pending workers? :eyes:

ana_runtime: Checking metrics — GPU util ~98% on pool, autoscaler didn't spin up because burst-capacity flag was off for that pool. Also seeing a lot of very long prefixes in requests so batching holds the KV cache longer and increases latency for following requests.

mike_oncall: Short mitigation plan: enable burst-capacity on the pool, temporarily reduce max_batch_size for that tenant to avoid head-of-line blocking, and enable fast-fail routing to a quantized fallback model for non-critical requests. Who can run the changes? :hammer:

ana_runtime: Doing it now. Patch commands: 
`````
redwoodctl pools update --pool acme-prod --burst-capacity true
redwoodctl routes set --tenant acme --fallback-model redwood-7b-q4f16 --max-batch-size 1
`````
Applying...

ana_runtime: Done. Routing updated and burst-capacity toggled.

josh_support: Notified customer with the change and asked them to repro. I opened INC-21345 and attached trace: https://traces.prod/redwood/txn/0a1b2c

acme_ops: Customer side confirm — p99 dropped to ~1.1s within 3 minutes, p95 now ~350ms. Looks much better, thanks. :tada:

mike_oncall: Preliminary root cause: (1) burst disabled on a reserved pool, (2) tenant had large max_batch_size and sustained long-prefix requests causing head-of-line blocking and queue growth, (3) autoscaler threshold was conservative.

mike_oncall: Follow-ups: update autoscaler policy to allow reactive scale when queue_len>30 for >60s, add tenant-fairness rule to limit max inflight per-tenant to 100, and add an alert when admission queue_len>50 for >2m. I'll file PRs.

shannon_pm: Please coordinate with sales/customer-success for a short credit and schedule a 1-hr RCA with ACME. I'll own the postmortem doc and customer comms.

ana_runtime: I'll upload metrics + timeline to the incident doc and include the redwoodctl commands, traces, and the exact patch diff. Moving to #postmortems once stable. :white_check_mark:
